title: The spectral reduction for the double ergodic averages along non-polynomial sequences
author: Rongzhong Xiao
work: Pointwise convergence of double ergodic averages along certain non-polynomial sequences
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: original Proposition 3.2 of the article (source label prop3:scalar, source0.tex lines 1008--1018), the spectral reduction that bounds the squared $L^2$-norm of the double average of the shifted functions $F(S^{\alpha R u})G(S^{\beta R u})$ by the average of the supremum of the spectral multiplier $|\mathcal A_h(\xi)|$, delivered with the author’s own complete 128-line proof at source0.tex lines 1019--1146. H2: the proof is a genuine spectral-theoretic reduction rather than a qualifying examination exercise. The solver must choose measurable representatives for the cut-off kernels, expand the double average through the Fourier multiplier representation, pass to the spectral measure of the underlying measure-preserving system, dominate the resulting oscillatory integral by the supremum of the multiplier through the Folland kernel estimate quoted from the delivered bibliography entry, and keep the constants uniform in the interval $I_0$ and in $H$. Obtaining the sharp bound in $H$ that the main theorem needs, from a double average along two non-polynomial sequences, is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying level.
